data.cultural_impact: The name Shalabh holds significant cultural importance in Hindu mythology, particularly in the context of the Mahabharata. Shalabh is the name of one of the Panchala king's sons, Vibhishana, who later becomes a key ally of Lord Rama during his exile and eventual battle against the demon King Ravana to rescue his wife Sita. The name symbolizes courage, loyalty, and wisdom, which are important values in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: At a deeper spiritual level, the name Shalabh can be understood as a reminder of one's inner strength and ability to overcome challenges. It encourages individuals to tap into their inner resources and face adversity with courage and resilience. The name also embodies the concept of Shakti or power within, reminding us that each one of us has the potential to conquer our weaknesses and inner demons. By embracing the name Shalabh, one can affirm their commitment to spiritual growth and personal development.

historical_references.reference: Shalabh was a king mentioned in the Hindu epic Mahabharata, who ruled the kingdom of Madra. He was a powerful warrior and a friend of the Pandava brothers.

historical_references.reference: Shalabh is also mentioned in Jain texts as a ruler of the Anavattha region. He is known for his patronage of Jain monks and his role in the spread of Jainism during the 6th century BCE.
